newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom tightens share trade rules.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom tightens share trade rules.

text.p: Russia's natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom, whose shares have fallen one third in value this week, has tightened the rules restricting shareholders' rights to trade its shares, a company official said on Wednesday.
Under company rules, shareholders have to offer any shares they want to sell to the company before they sell them to another party.
In the past the company had up to 30 days to buy the shares, otherwise shareholders were free to sell them to whoever they wanted with no further limits.

Now shareholders must sell their shares within 90 days of the 30-day limit expiring. If they fail to do so they must reapply to Gazprom for permission to sell, Gazprom securities department head Eduard Ivanov told Reuters.
Gazprom is Russia's biggest company by market capitalisation, but the restrictions make its shares extremely illiquid.
Gazprom shares nevertheless have fallen sharply on the Russian Trading System in the last two days. They closed at $0.300 on Wednesday, down from $0.355 on Tuesday, and $0.445 on Monday.
Some traders said the fall of one third this week in Gazprom shares was due to the new restrictions.

But Ivanov said the main reason was that a large number of shares from outside Moscow had been put up for sale a month ago when prices were high. These sales were now going through, and this was depressing the share price.
